The objective content of revelation is not diminished by the subjective failure of those who reject it.

Point 2. Grace is never canceled by the failure of those who reject grace. The potential for greatness through grace remains intact regardless of how many individuals or generations turn away from it.

Point 3. Grace is never neutralized by what others do or fail to do. This principle has immediate application to the individual believer living through historical disaster: the failure of the surrounding culture, the collapse of national institutions, the spread of negative volition — none of these conditions alter the capacity of the plan of God to bless the individual who maintains positive volition toward doctrine. The book of Daniel illustrates this across an entire career lived under the most adverse historical conditions.

Point 4. Grace continues as the policy of the justice of God in imputing blessing to the divine righteousness resident in the mature believer. Blessing from God is available under any historical circumstances to any believer who continues in sustained positive volition toward doctrine after salvation.

Point 5. Man's failure cannot abrogate divine integrity. God's faithfulness is grounded in His own character, not in the performance of those He has blessed. This is the basis for hope in times of national decline.

Point 6. Lack of integrity in mankind does not cancel the integrity of God.

Point 7. Man may cultivate and acquire a form of integrity — moral character, self-discipline, civic virtue — but such acquired integrity is not the righteousness that God's system requires. The self-made man operates on the axle of self-righteousness, which is acceptable to other men and forms the basis of human social approval, but which cannot access the pipeline of divine blessing.

Point 8. God's integrity consists of two components: divine righteousness and divine justice. Righteousness demands righteousness; justice demands justice. The resolution is the judicial imputation of God's righteousness to the believer at salvation: what righteousness demands, justice executes. When the righteousness of God imputed to the believer reaches maturity through maximum doctrine resident in the soul, righteousness demands blessing from justice, and justice imputes that blessing through the pipeline. This principle holds in depression, in prosperity, in historical disaster, and in historical triumph. The believer who follows the plan of God is blessed in the worst of circumstances.

Point 9. Justification can only occur when God imputes His righteousness — one half of divine integrity — to mankind. This imputation occurs at the moment of salvation through faith in Christ (Romans 5:1: 'Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ').

VII. Paul's Burden — The Decisive Alternative

The first four verses of Romans 9, and the entire body of theological analysis they have generated, converge on a single decisive alternative. Paul's burden is this:

Either the Jew will adjust to the justice of God through faith in Jesus Christ, or the justice of God will adjust to the Jew through temporal and eternal judgment.

There is no third option. The Lord Jesus Christ is the only Savior: 'Neither is there salvation in any other, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved' (Acts 4:12). Positive volition — believing in Christ — is the non-meritorious expression of free will that results in eternal life and, in the present dispensation, incorporation into the royal family of God. In the previous dispensation, it resulted in the fulfillment of the promises of the unconditional covenants, which will be realized in full at the second advent and through the millennium into eternity.

Negative volition — rejecting Christ as Savior — means judgment in time and judgment in eternity. The greatness of Israel's heritage intensifies rather than mitigates the weight of that rejection. The unconditional covenants — the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, and New Covenant to Israel — have never been fulfilled and will not be fulfilled until the second advent. Their fulfillment requires eternal life. The imputation of eternal life at salvation is therefore the indispensable foundation for inheriting everything the heritage of Israel promises. Physical descent from Abraham without the new birth means exclusion from the very inheritance the physical descent seems to guarantee.

Point 8 of the Jewish problem must be held alongside all that precedes it: the failure of some Jews does not cancel or abrogate the faithfulness of God. God's faithfulness to Israel will continue throughout history and will reach its climax at the second advent and in the fulfillment of the unconditional covenants to believing Israel.

Point 9. While every generation has its unbelievers, such unbelief does not cancel the integrity of God or neutralize His faithfulness to those who do believe. The remnant principle is always operative: grace is never without a witness.

Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Four

1. The Mosaic Law has three distinct divisions: the commandments (freedom code), the ordinances (theological code), and the judgments (establishment code). Each serves a different function; conflating them has been a persistent source of theological error in both Jewish and Christian interpretation.

2. The ordinances form the true spiritual heritage of Israel, because they contain a complete soteriology and Christology presented through the Levitical ritual system. Every element of the ordinances is a shadow whose reality is the person and work of the Lord Jesus Christ.

3. The Mosaic Law cannot justify, cannot give eternal life, cannot provide the filling of the Holy Spirit, and cannot solve the problem of the old sin nature. These limitations are not defects in the law but are intrinsic to its design: the law was never intended to do these things but to point to the one who does.

4. Physical descent from Abraham is not the basis of spiritual standing. The line of Israel is defined by spiritual seed — faith in the Lord Jesus Christ — as demonstrated successively by the exclusion of Nahor, the selection of Isaac over Ishmael, and the selection of Jacob over Esau. The pattern is established in Genesis 15:6.

5. The new birth involves two simultaneous judicial imputations: divine righteousness imputed to the believer, establishing the target for all blessing from God in time; and eternal life imputed to the human spirit, newly created by the Holy Spirit at regeneration. Both are necessary for the fulfillment of the unconditional covenants in eternity.

6. The Shekinah glory was the visible presence of the Lord Jesus Christ — Jehovah Elohim — dwelling among His people. The mercy seat, flanked by the cherubim of righteousness and justice, depicted propitiation: the satisfaction of divine integrity by the blood that typologically represented the future work of Christ on the cross.

7. The Jewish problem is a structured theological failure: ritual without reality, producing arrogance and self-righteousness, leading to the assumption that human compliance with an external code is equivalent to the divine righteousness that the code reveals to be unattainable by human effort. The law's own purpose — to drive the sinner to Christ — is inverted.

8. Self-righteousness cannot access the pipeline of divine blessing. All blessing from God flows from the justice of God to the righteousness of God imputed in the believer who has reached maturity through maximum doctrine resident in the soul. No form of human self-righteousness — whether Jewish legalism, moralism, social activism, or Christian works-based thinking — can intrude into this system.

9. Grace is never neutralized by the failure of those who reject it. Man's failure cannot abrogate divine integrity. The plan of God rolls on regardless of historical conditions, and the believer who maintains positive volition toward doctrine is blessed under any circumstances of life.

10. The decisive alternative that constitutes Paul's burden: either the Jew adjusts to the justice of God through faith in Jesus Christ, or the justice of God adjusts to the Jew through temporal and eternal judgment. The Lord Jesus Christ is Jehovah Elohim — identical in person, distinguished only by the language and dispensational context of revelation.

11. The failure of individual Jews or of entire generations does not abrogate the faithfulness of God to Israel. The unconditional covenants will be fulfilled at the second advent and through the millennium into eternity, but only for believing Israel — those who share the faith of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

12. Justification is a judicial act of God, not an attainment of man. God imputes His own righteousness to the believer at the moment of faith in Christ (Romans 5:1). This imputation, constituting one half of divine integrity in the believer, is the indispensable precondition for all subsequent blessing in the plan of God.

Glossary

Term Greek / Transliteration Definition
Shekinah שְׁכִינָה shekinah — the dwelling presence From the Hebrew verb shakan — to dwell, to tabernacle. The luminous divine presence that hovered between the cherubim above the mercy seat of the Ark of the Covenant. Theologically, the visible manifestation of the presence of the Lord Jesus Christ (Jehovah Elohim) dwelling among Israel. Related term: kavod (כָּבוֹד) — the glory or weightiness of the divine presence.
kavod כָּבוֹד kavod — glory, weight, honor The Hebrew term for divine glory, often paired with the Shekinah presence. Denotes the weightiness, honor, and manifest splendor of God's character and presence. In the context of Romans 9:4, the 'glory' (Greek doxa) given to Israel as a privilege is the Shekinah-kavod — the visible presence of God among the nation.
Tetelestai Τετέλεσται tetelestai — it is finished, it stands completed Perfect passive indicative of the Greek verb teleō — to complete, to bring to an end. The declaration of the Lord Jesus Christ on the cross (John 19:30), signifying that the work of salvation is a closed, completed transaction. Nothing can be added to it and nothing subtracted from it; any condition added to faith for salvation contradicts this declaration.
Kyrios Iēsous Christos Κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός Kyrios Iēsous Christos — Lord Jesus Christ The Greek title of the Lord Jesus Christ, synonymous with the Hebrew Adonai Elohim (Jehovah Elohim). The identity of the God of Israel with the Lord Jesus Christ is the theological foundation of Paul's burden in Romans 9: to believe in Jehovah in the previous dispensation was to believe in the same person as the Lord Jesus Christ in the present dispensation.
dikaiosynē theou δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ dikaiosynē theou — righteousness of God The righteousness that belongs to God by nature, and which is judicially imputed to the believer at the moment of faith in Christ. As the target or 'home' for all blessing from God, it establishes the grace pipeline through which the justice of God channels blessing to imperfect man without compromising the divine attributes. Central organizing axis of the Epistle to the Romans.
epignosis ἐπίγνωσις epignosis — full, exact knowledge The category of knowledge required for spiritual growth beyond gnosis (notional understanding). Epignosis is Bible doctrine that has been received under the filling of the Holy Spirit through the Grace Apparatus for Perception (GAP) and metabolized into the right lobe of the soul as the basis for spiritual momentum toward maturity.
old sin nature (OSN) The sin capacity inherited by every member of the human race at physical birth through the male genetic line, originating in Adam's original sin. Adam's original sin is judicially imputed to the OSN as its genetically prepared home, establishing universal condemnation as the precondition for salvation. The OSN contains an area of strength (producing human good and self-righteousness) and an area of weakness (producing personal sins), as well as trends toward asceticism or licentiousness.
five cycles of discipline Progressive stages of national divine discipline described in Leviticus 26, applied to Israel as a client nation for sustained maladjustment to the justice of God. The fifth cycle is the most severe: total removal from client nation status through military conquest, dispersion, and loss of national sovereignty. Administered to the Northern Kingdom through Assyria (722 BC), to the Southern Kingdom through Babylon (586 BC), and finally through Rome in AD 70, inaugurating the times of the Gentiles.
times of the Gentiles The period extending from the Roman destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70 through the second advent of Christ, during which only a Gentile nation can serve as a client nation to God. Encompasses the church age and the tribulation. Israel resumes its client nation function at the second advent with the fulfillment of the unconditional covenants.
maturity adjustment The third and most advanced category of adjustment to the justice of God, achieved through maximum doctrine resident in the soul after sustained positive volition toward Bible teaching over time. Produces the crossing of the maturity barrier into supergrace and ultra-supergrace, at which point the justice of God imputes blessing through the divine righteousness imputed at salvation. Distinct from salvation adjustment (instantaneous, at faith in Christ) and rebound adjustment (instantaneous, repeated; 1 John 1:9).

Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Five

Romans 9:4 — Concluding Summary: The Integrity of God and the Spiritual Heritage of Israel

Romans 9:4 “They are Israelites, and to them belong the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the worship, and the promises.” (ESV)
Corrected translation: Who are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption and the Shekinah glory and the unconditional covenants and the gift of the law and the worship and the promises.

Romans 9 continues Paul's extended treatment of Israel's place within the plan of God. Verse 4 catalogues the spiritual heritage given to Israel — adoption, the Shekinah glory, the unconditional covenants, the law, the temple worship, and the promises. Over the preceding sessions this heritage has been examined piece by piece. This chapter draws those threads together into a unified doctrinal summary organized around the integrity of God as the operative principle behind every element of Israel's heritage, and as the axis around which the plan of God for both Israel and the royal family of God turns.

I. The Integrity of God: Foundation of the Heritage

The spiritual heritage listed in Romans 9:4 is not intelligible apart from a prior understanding of the God who granted it. Every element of that heritage — adoption, the Shekinah glory, the covenants, the law, the worship, the promises — flows from who and what God is. The starting point, therefore, is the holiness of God.

A. The Nature of Divine Holiness

God is holy. Holiness is the integrity of God, comprising both His righteousness and His justice. This integrity was neither attained nor developed; it is the eternal, absolute, infinite self of God. There has never been a decline in His integrity, nor an increase. God as eternal Being has always possessed perfect righteousness and perfect justice without variation.

The integrity of God is not the mere absence of evil. It is the sum total of His perfection — the explanation of His perfect consistency, His stability, and His honorable dealing with the human race. The being of God cannot be better or worse, for God is eternal, immutable, unalterable, and absolute Being who is eternally consistent. God has never been inconsistent — not even once.

B. Righteousness and Justice as the Two Components of Divine Integrity

Divine holiness is composed of two essential attributes: righteousness and justice. God's righteousness is perfect. It therefore not only rejects sin, human good, and evil, but also provides the varying systems by which condemnation and punishment are administered to sin, human good, and evil. God's justice is perfect, and therefore demands perfection. It is never arbitrary and never unfair. It is always absolute and total perfection in the administration of either punitive action or the imputation of blessing.

The governing principle is this: what the righteousness of God demands, the justice of God executes. God's righteousness can only demand perfect righteousness. God's justice can only execute perfect justice. The justice of God is therefore the believer's point of reference — and it was equally Israel's point of reference, forming the basis for the entire spiritual heritage catalogued in Romans 9:4. This is the dikaiosynē theou (δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ), the righteousness of God, which is not a standard imposed from outside but the very self of God in its consistency toward the creature.

II. The Shekinah Glory: Invisible Presence Made Visible

Among the elements of Israel's heritage, the Shekinah glory is theologically central because it is the one element that bridges Old Testament typology, the first advent, and the present dispensation.

A. The Shekinah in the Tabernacle

In Hebrew the term is shekhinah (שְׁכִינָה), from the root meaning to dwell or to tabernacle. The Shekinah glory was the personal, invisible presence of the Lord Jesus Christ dwelling between the cherubim above the mercy seat of the Ark of the Covenant in the Holy of Holies. The two cherubim represented the holiness of God — one standing for the righteousness of God, the other for the justice of God.

Access to the Holy of Holies was restricted. The Levitical priesthood could enter the Holy Place, but only the high priest could enter the Holy of Holies, and only once a year on the Day of Atonement. On that day blood was sprinkled over the mercy seat. The righteousness of God saw the blood and was satisfied. The justice of God saw the blood and was satisfied. This was a typological portrayal of propitiation — the propitiatory work of Christ on the cross by which the integrity of God was fully satisfied with respect to the sins of the human race.

Outside the veil stood the table of showbread, the lampstand, and the altar of incense — all pointing to the one behind the veil. Outside the tabernacle stood the bronze altar with its continual sacrifices in five categories, each portraying a different facet of the person and work of the Lord Jesus Christ. The great feasts of Israel — Passover, Unleavened Bread, Firstfruits, Pentecost, Trumpets, Atonement, Tabernacles — all converged on the same Person. No Israelite could legitimately claim ignorance of the one the entire system portrayed.

B. The Shekinah in the First Advent

The Shekinah glory became visible in the incarnation. The eternal second Person of the Trinity, possessing all the divine attributes, entered the human race through true humanity. The glory of God was visible through the miracles of Christ and through His teaching — the hypostatic union, the God-man, was the Shekinah glory no longer concealed behind a veil but present and observable.

Throughout Israel's history a recurring rationalization had been offered: the people could not see God; how could they be held accountable? When Israel fell into reversionism the pattern was consistent — the manufacture of idols from stone, wood, bronze, gold, or silver, the claim being that worship required a visible object. The first advent answered that rationalization definitively. For thirty-three years the Shekinah glory was on the earth in visible form. The Jews saw His miracles. They heard His message. They had the complete picture. The response of the nation's leadership was nevertheless the same sustained negative volition that had characterized Israel's reversionism throughout the Old Testament period. This demonstrates that the physical presence of God in the world makes no difference to negative volition. The issue is never proximity to the divine presence; the issue is always the volitional attitude of the soul toward truth.

C. The Shekinah, Propitiation, and the Two Judicial Imputations

The connection between the Shekinah glory and the work of the cross is not incidental. The mercy seat over the Ark was the typological locus of propitiation. In order for propitiation to become an actual historical event rather than a repeated annual ritual, the Shekinah glory had to become flesh. By becoming true humanity, the second Person of the Trinity acquired the capacity to receive the judicial imputation of the sins of the entire human race and to be judged for them by God the Father.

This explains the mechanics of two judicial imputations that stand apart from all real imputations. A judicial imputation has only one factor — there is no antecedent home or target in the recipient. All personal sins of all human history were imputed to Christ on the cross; there was no home for them in His perfect humanity — they were placed there by judicial imputation. The tearing of the temple veil from top to bottom at the moment of His death is the architectural announcement that the typology has been fulfilled.

The second judicial imputation is the imputation of divine righteousness to the believer at the moment of faith in Christ. There is no antecedent righteousness in the human soul that could serve as a target; there is no righteousness producible by moral effort, legal observance, or any form of human performance. The imputation is therefore judicial — granted by the justice of God on the basis of the completed work of Christ, not on the basis of anything in the recipient. This is justification. The imputed righteousness of God becomes the permanent qualification for all subsequent divine blessing.

III. The Plan of God: Three Adjustments and Seven Imputations

The heritage of Israel, rightly understood, was designed to bring Israel to justification through faith in Christ — not to provide a basis for national arrogance or personal self-righteousness. The failure of Israel was the failure to see the heritage in terms of divine doctrine rather than human history. The same heritage, now transmitted to the royal family of God in the Church Age, provides the motivational foundation for spiritual advance. Its structure is the plan of God expressed in three adjustments and seven imputations.

A. The Three Imputations of Common Grace and Salvation

At physical birth, human life is imputed to the soul — this is the first imputation, a real imputation where human life finds its home in the soul. Simultaneously, Adam's original sin is imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature — the second imputation, which establishes the first potentiality: the need for salvation. The gospel then constitutes the third element of the first stage: doctrine in the form of the gospel message, which, when believed, triggers the salvation adjustment to the justice of God. At that moment the judicial imputation of divine righteousness occurs, and eternal life is imputed to the human spirit through regeneration.

B. The Second Stage: Maturity Adjustment

Following salvation, the continued intake of Bible doctrine through the Grace Apparatus for Perception moves the believer through the Y-axis of the plan — from salvation toward spiritual maturity. The maturity adjustment to the justice of God is reached when maximum doctrine is resident in the soul. This is the point at which the divine imputation of blessing in time occurs — six categories of temporal blessing that have no relationship to logistical grace. Logistical grace is God's provision of everything necessary for physical existence: food, shelter, clothing, transportation, the freedom to assemble, and pastors who communicate doctrine. These provisions sustain life; they are not blessings in the technical sense. Blessing in the technical sense requires capacity, and capacity is produced only through doctrine resident in the soul.

C. The Third Stage: Ultra-Supergrace and Eternal Blessing

Beyond the maturity adjustment, the continuation of doctrine intake combined with providentially assigned undeserved suffering — suffering that does not arise from personal sin or divine discipline but is assigned as a means of grace — produces focus on eternity. This focus, the third absolute confidence, corresponds to the seventh imputation: the imputation of blessing in eternity, which glorifies God forever. This is the ultimate purpose of the plan of God. There is no human work, no system of self-generated righteousness, no sacrifice of personality or possessions that produces this result. It is produced exclusively by Bible doctrine, more Bible doctrine, and more Bible doctrine.

IV. Self-Righteousness Versus Imputed Righteousness

The failure of Israel in Romans 9 is paradigmatically the failure of self-righteousness. Arrogance combined with self-righteousness rejects the plan of God — not only in the case of Israel, but in the case of any believer in any dispensation. Human self-righteousness is an arrogant rationalization: the fantasy of comparing one's own strengths against the weaknesses of others, and concluding from that comparison that one possesses a righteousness acceptable to God.

Righteousness cannot be built on unrighteousness. Justification is built on the imputed righteousness of God, not on any system of self-righteousness that the creature has developed. To impute blessing to any system of self-righteousness would constitute a compromise of the essence of God — and that is logically impossible. God cannot compromise His own integrity. The self-righteous type is in effect attempting to compete with God, which is tantamount to blasphemous arrogance.

A useful analogy: the plan of God is a wheel that turns on the axle of imputed divine righteousness. Self-righteousness is the wrong axle. It cannot support the wheel. When a believer substitutes self-righteousness for imputed righteousness as the operational basis of the Christian life, the result is legalism — man by his own efforts attempting to secure divine approbation or derived blessing. This takes many forms: tithing conceived as a mechanism of securing blessing, witnessing performed as a work for which God is expected to reward the performer, asceticism, personality improvement, and moral reformation. None of these produce the righteousness God recognizes, because none of them are the righteousness God imputes.

The grace of God provides all that the integrity of God demands for the human race through the God of Israel, the Lord Jesus Christ. This is the basis for the spiritual heritage of Israel and equally for the spiritual heritage of the Church as the royal family of God. Grace is the policy of the justice of God in imputing blessing from the justice of God to the righteousness of God resident in the believer. It operates exclusively within that framework and nowhere else.

V. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Divine Initiative

The pattern of God giving and man receiving — not man giving and God gaining — is embedded in the very origin of the Jewish race. Abraham was a Sumero-Akkadian Gentile. The Jewish race did not originate in the X-axis of physical birth and the common heritage of all humanity. It originated in the Z-axis, in the ultra-supergrace of Abraham after he had cracked the maturity barrier at the age of one hundred.

Genesis 15:6 states: he believed in the Lord, and it was imputed to him for righteousness. The Hebrew verb is he'emin (הֶאֱמִין), the Hiphil perfect of aman — to exercise faith, to believe with confidence. The imputation that followed was judicial: divine righteousness credited to Abraham's account on the basis of non-meritorious faith. Abraham did nothing to earn it. The Jewish race was therefore born from a spiritual transaction, not a physical one. Its origin is in the Z-axis, not the X-axis. Jews who appeal to the physical genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as a basis for standing before God have misidentified the very category in which their heritage is located.

This establishes the foundational principle: God does not gain from man; man gains from God. There is no point in angelic history or human history where the integrity of God has been compromised by gaining anything from the creature. God's righteousness is not established by man; man's integrity is established by God. God does not need human help. The believer benefits from the integrity of God; the integrity of God does not benefit from the believer.

VI. The Law: Condemnation, Not Salvation

The Mosaic Law occupies a prominent place in the heritage of Romans 9:4, but it must be understood in its proper function. The law is both spiritual and an instrument of establishment — it delineates principles of freedom, privacy, property, and authority; it portrays the person of Christ through its ritual system. It was never, however, an instrument of salvation.

The law demands a perfection beyond the ability of fallen man. It cannot produce in the Jew any righteousness equivalent to the perfect and eternal righteousness of God. What the law can do — and does with precision — is condemn. It demonstrates the Jew's inadequacy to save himself. The law is an instrument of condemnation; only the judgment of Christ on the cross is the instrument of salvation. Israel's failure at this precise point — treating the law as a means of righteousness rather than recognizing it as a pointer to Christ — is the failure Paul addresses in Romans 9–11.

VII. The Priority of the Jew in the Present Dispensation

Paul frames the gospel in Romans as addressed 'to the Jew first and also to the Greek' (Romans 1:16). This ordering is not arbitrary and does not imply that Jewish unbelievers have a superior position before God. It reflects two historical realities of the present dispensation.

First, the one who hung on the cross was the Son of David, the fulfillment of the Davidic covenant, the visible Shekinah glory in hypostatic union. The Lord Jesus Christ in His humanity is a Jew. He is the prince-ruler of the Church. Second, the primary human author of New Testament theology is the Apostle Paul, a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin, trained in the Old Testament scriptures and in possession of the fullest understanding of the plan of God ever given to a member of the human race outside of the Lord Jesus Christ Himself. The theological heritage of the Old Testament, transmitted through Jewish writers and culminating in Paul's thirteen epistles, provides the Church with its motivational and doctrinal foundation for spiritual advance. The priority of the Jew is therefore not ethnic privilege but historical function within the plan of God.

Israel is currently under the fifth cycle of discipline. The client nation responsibility has passed to those Gentile nations that have received the word of God and provided the conditions for its free communication. The Church age believer who understands Israel's failures profits from them, avoiding the same errors of self-righteousness, arrogance, and negative volition that brought the fifth cycle upon Israel.

VIII. Foreknowledge and Omniscience Distinguished

Romans 9 in its subsequent verses will require a precise distinction between divine omniscience and divine foreknowledge — two attributes that are not synonymous and are never used interchangeably in Scripture.

Omniscience is the attribute of God by which He knows simultaneously and eternally everything that is actual, everything that is possible, and everything that could have been but was not. In theology, what God knows as having actually occurred is called actuality; what could have occurred but did not is called the scientia media or middle knowledge — the knowledge of contingent possibilities. Omniscience fed all actual information into the divine decrees, which are the computer of God's eternal plan containing only what does, in fact, occur in history.

Foreknowledge — prognōsis (πρόγνωσις) — is categorically distinct. Foreknowledge makes nothing certain. Foreknowledge merely acknowledges what is already certain on the basis of the divine decrees. It is a recognition of what is in the decrees, not the cause of what is in the decrees. To treat foreknowledge as equivalent to omniscience collapses the distinction between God's knowledge of possibilities and His recognition of actualities. This distinction will be critical for understanding the subsequent arguments of Romans 9 regarding election, predestination, and the sovereign dealings of God with Israel and the nations.

Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Five

1. God is holy — that is, God has integrity. The holiness of God comprises both His perfect righteousness and His perfect justice. This integrity was neither attained nor developed; it is the eternal, immutable, absolute self of God. It has never increased and has never declined.

2. The integrity of God is the operative principle behind every element of Israel's heritage. Adoption, Shekinah glory, unconditional covenants, the law, worship, and promises are all expressions of the integrity of God directed toward Israel as His client nation.

3. What the righteousness of God demands, the justice of God executes. God's righteousness demands perfect righteousness; since no member of the human race possesses it, the justice of God executes judgment on sin. The solution is judicial imputation: divine righteousness credited to the believer at salvation through non-meritorious faith in Christ.

4. The Shekinah glory is the personal presence of the Lord Jesus Christ. In the Mosaic economy it was invisible, dwelling between the cherubim behind the veil of the Holy of Holies. In the first advent it became visible in hypostatic union — true humanity united with undiminished deity — so that the nation of Israel could no longer plead the excuse of never having seen God.

5. The presence of the Shekinah glory does not alter negative volition. Israel's sustained rejection of Christ during the first advent demonstrates that physical proximity to the divine presence produces no change in those who are negative toward divine truth. The issue is always the volitional attitude of the soul toward Bible doctrine, not external circumstances.

6. The incarnation was necessary for propitiation. The mercy seat in the Holy of Holies was the typological location of propitiation. For propitiation to become a historical reality, the Shekinah glory had to acquire true humanity so that the judicial imputation of all human sin could be executed against Him on the cross. The tearing of the temple veil announced the fulfillment of the type.

7. Two judicial imputations have no antecedent home in the recipient. The imputation of all human sins to Christ on the cross, and the imputation of divine righteousness to the believer at salvation, are both judicial — granted by the justice of God without any corresponding target in the recipient. Both are essential to the plan of God and neither can be replicated by human effort.

8. Self-righteousness is the wrong axle for the plan of God. Any attempt to substitute human moral achievement, legal observance, or religious performance for the imputed righteousness of God as the basis of the Christian life is legalism. It cannot produce what only judicial imputation provides. The plan of God turns on the axle of imputed divine righteousness; self-righteousness cannot bear the load.

9. God does not gain from man; man gains from God. The very origin of the Jewish race illustrates this principle. Abraham's justification in Genesis 15:6 was a judicial imputation of divine righteousness on the basis of non-meritorious faith. The Jewish race was born in the Z-axis of ultra-supergrace, not in the X-axis of physical generation. God initiated; Abraham received.

10. The law is an instrument of condemnation, not salvation. The Mosaic Law portrays the person of Christ and establishes principles of freedom and order, but it demands a perfection no fallen human being can produce. Its function is to demonstrate the inadequacy of human righteousness and point to the one who alone satisfies its demands.

11. The integrity of God advances the glory of God through all of history. With all the failure of angelic history and all the failure and degeneration of human history, the integrity of God advances the glory of God. Under divine provision man can glorify God, but man cannot advance the glory of God. The glory of God pre-existed all creatures, including the angels.

12. Foreknowledge and omniscience are not synonymous. Omniscience is the divine attribute by which God knows all actualities and all contingent possibilities simultaneously and eternally. Foreknowledge recognizes what is already certain in the divine decrees but makes nothing certain. Conflating the two terms produces confusion in the interpretation of Romans 9 on election and predestination.

13. The spiritual heritage of Israel has been transmitted to the royal family of God. The Church, as the body of Church Age believers, receives the theological heritage of Israel — including its covenants, its Shekinah typology, and its pattern of adjustment to the justice of God — as motivational and doctrinal foundation for advance to spiritual maturity. Israel's failures serve as a cautionary framework; Israel's heritage serves as a gift.

Glossary

propitiation ἱλαστήριον hilastērion — mercy seat; propitiatory sacrifice The satisfaction of the righteousness and justice of God with respect to human sin, accomplished by the judicial imputation of all personal sins to Christ on the cross and their subsequent judgment by God the Father. hypostatic union The union of full, undiminished deity and true, complete humanity in the one person of Jesus Christ. Neither nature is diminished, altered, or confused by the other. The visible Shekinah glory of the first advent is the hypostatic union.
adjustment to the justice of God The mechanism by which all divine blessing is received. Three categories: salvation adjustment (faith in Christ at the moment of salvation); rebound adjustment (naming known sins to God, restoring fellowship, 1 John 1:9); and maturity adjustment (maximum doctrine resident in the soul, producing the capacity for divine blessing in time and eternity).
logistical grace God's provision of everything necessary for the believer's physical existence in time: food, shelter, clothing, transportation, freedom, and access to Bible doctrine. Distinct from blessing, which requires the capacity produced by doctrine resident in the soul.
maturity adjustment The third category of adjustment to the justice of God. Reached through the sustained daily intake of Bible doctrine over time, culminating in maximum doctrine resident in the soul. The threshold at which the justice of God imputes temporal blessing to the righteousness of God in the mature believer.
he'emin הֶאֱמִין he'emin — he believed Hiphil perfect of the Hebrew root aman, meaning to be firm, reliable, or faithful. In Genesis 15:6, Abraham 'believed in the Lord,' and divine righteousness was imputed to him. The paradigmatic text for justification by faith in the Old Testament.
old sin nature (OSN) The sin capacity inherited at physical birth through the male genetic line. Adam's original sin is imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature at birth.
