Used of God's foreordination of the believer to a specific destiny in union with Christ. Distinguished from the noun prothesis by its verbal, action-oriented emphasis.
protithēmi προτίθημι protithēmi — to set forth beforehand, to purpose Verb. From pro (before) + tithēmi (to place). Emphasizes the provision side of God's predetermined plan: that God placed in the decrees not only the facts about believers but the full logistical support for every believer's advance through the plan of God. Used in Romans 3:25 of God's setting forth of propitiation.
prognōsis / proginōskō πρόγνωσις / προγινώσκω prognōsis / proginōskō — foreknowledge / to foreknow Noun and verb. Not a predictive knowledge that precedes and determines the decrees, but an acknowledgment of what omniscience has already placed in the decrees. Foreknowledge is the printout; omniscience feeds the computer. Applies exclusively to the actual, never to the possible or probable.
ekloge ἐκλογή eklogē — election, selection Noun. From eklegomai (to select, to choose out). The printout from the divine decrees concerning believers. Operates at two levels: individual (each believing person as elect) and collective (Israel, the church, the millennial saints as elected bodies). Never applied to unbelievers in Scripture.
dikaiosynē theou δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ dikaiosynē theou — righteousness of God The central subject of the Epistle to the Romans. The perfect righteousness that belongs to God as a component of His essence and that is imputed judicially to the believer at salvation. The target of all divine blessing; without it no creature can receive anything from the justice of God.
anthropopathism anthropopathismos — ascription of human emotion to God A figure of speech in which a human emotional response is ascribed to God for the purpose of communicating a divine truth in terms accessible to human comprehension. God does not possess emotions in the human sense; anthropopathisms accommodate the infinite to the finite without implying that God is subject to emotional states. 'God so loved the world' (John 3:16) and 'the Lord repented' (Genesis 6:6) are examples.
hypostatic union hypostatikē henōsis The permanent union of full deity and true humanity in the one person of Jesus Christ. The Shekinah glory — the visible manifestation of the second person of the Trinity — became flesh and tabernacled among men (John 1:14) in the only form in which the invisible God could be seen: the God-man.
logistical grace God's provision of everything necessary for the believer's continued physical existence and spiritual advance in time. Incorporated into the divine decrees as part of foreordination: God decreed not only that there would be believers but that they would be fully supplied with every resource needed to execute the plan of God.
old sin nature (OSN) The sin capacity formed genetically in every member of the human race through the male genetic line. Adam's original sin is imputed to it at birth. It is the source of personal sins, human good, and evil — all of which are unacceptable to the righteousness of God and condemned by the justice of God.
client nation A national entity that fulfills specific divine purposes in a given dispensation: maintaining freedom under the laws of divine establishment, supporting Bible teaching, conducting evangelism, and providing a base for missionary activity. Israel was the first client nation; during the times of the Gentiles (70 AD to the Second Advent), only Gentile nations can serve in this role.
supralapsarianism supralapsarianismos The theological position that God decreed the fall and the damnation of the reprobate as positive ends prior to and independent of His decree to create. Rejected by the present commentary as inconsistent with the biblical data: God is not the author of sin; human self-determination is the cause of sin; and no unbeliever is predestined or foreordained to hell.
maturity adjustment The third category of adjustment to the justice of God, achieved through sustained daily intake of Bible doctrine over time. Culminates in the believer cracking the maturity barrier and advancing to supergrace and ultra-supergrace, at which point the sixth imputation — temporal blessing to the righteousness of God — is activated.

Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Six

Romans 9:10 — The Integrity of God: Divine Love, Anthropopathisms, and the Justice of God as Mankind's Point of Reference

Romans 9:6–7 “But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel, and not all are children of Abraham because they are his offspring, but 'Through Isaac shall your offspring be named.'” (ESV)
Corrected translation: But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are really Israel, and not all because they are Abraham's physical descendants are children of the inheritance, but: In Isaac your seed shall be designated.

Romans 9 continues Paul's sustained argument that the word of God has not failed with respect to Israel. Chapter 576 remains within the extended doctrinal unit on the integrity of God — the thirteenth point in the doctrine of the Protocol Plan of God — and develops four sub-paragraphs: the divine attribute of love, the anthropopathism of love, mankind's point of reference as the justice of God, and human failure and the faithfulness of God. The chapter closes by introducing the pivot principle as it applies not merely to national preservation but to the perpetuation of the Jewish race across all generations of history.

I. The Divine Attribute of Love

The doctrine of the Protocol Plan of God, point thirteen, opens with the divine attribute of love. Before the anthropopathism of love can be understood, the actual attribute must be defined precisely, because confusion at this point corrupts every subsequent conclusion about how God relates to mankind.

A. The Nature of God's Love

God's love is complete, total, and eternally self-existent as part of the being of God. The statement of 1 John 4:8, 'God is love,' is a true predication of His essence. This means God does not fall in love, does not maintain love by an act of will, and His love is not sustained by emotion. It is an attribute — permanent, immutable, and entirely devoid of the emotional content that characterizes human love.

Two known objects of the divine attribute of love exist within the Godhead itself: (1) God's own perfect righteousness — an internal, subjective, and perfect love; (2) the other members of the Trinity — an external, objective, and perfect love. In righteousness, divine love for holiness is revealed. In justice, divine rejection of sin and evil is revealed.

The divine attribute of love requires a perfect object. All creatures are excluded from this attribute because of three disqualifying realities: (1) imputed sin — Adam's original sin credited to every member of the human race at birth; (2) the old sin nature inherited through the male genetic line; (3) the threefold manifestation of the old sin nature in sinfulness, human good, and evil. Perfect love, belonging to a perfect God, cannot be directed toward any of these.

Because the divine attribute of love does not require an object — unlike human love, which is generated by an object — God possesses this love whether any creature exists or not. In eternity past, the attribute existed in full. In eternity future, it will exist unchanged. The only human being who can become an object of the divine attribute of love is one who possesses God's own righteousness. That righteousness is imputed at the moment of faith in Christ. This is precisely what Romans is about.

Most scriptural references to God's love, however, do not address the divine attribute directly. They address the anthropopathism of love — a concept taken up in the following section.

II. The Anthropopathism of Love

A detailed treatment of anthropopathisms will accompany the exegesis of Romans 9:13. What follows is the preliminary framework needed to handle the key passage in advance.

A. Definition

An anthropopathism (ἀνθρωποπάθεια, anthrōpopatheia) is a human characteristic ascribed to God — a characteristic He does not actually possess — used to explain divine policy in terms of human motivation and human frame of reference. Because God is infinite and inscrutable, certain divine policies can only be communicated to finite minds through the medium of human experience. Attributes such as hatred, anger, repentance, and compassion are ascribed to God in Scripture not because He possesses them but because they describe His policy in terms that human beings can comprehend.

B. Romans 9:13 as the Classical Illustration

Romans 9:13 — 'Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated' — is the classical illustration of anthropopathic language. The text is regularly mistranslated because the definite article, functioning as a demonstrative pronoun, is ignored. A more precise rendering is: 'That Jacob I loved, but that Esau I hated.' God neither loves nor hates in human terms here. Two antithetical human characteristics — love and hate — are employed to explain a divine policy: salvation adjustment to the justice of God on one side, rejection of Christ as Savior on the other. The anthropopathism of love explains God's policy toward believing Jacob; the anthropopathism of hatred explains His policy toward unbelieving Esau.

C. Common Anthropopathisms of Love

Several familiar passages employ the anthropopathism of love rather than the divine attribute itself. John 3:16 is the most widely cited. Romans 5:8 and 2 Corinthians 9:7 are additional examples. These passages explain divine motivation in terms of human frame of reference, but the anthropopathism must not be confused with the attribute. Love as an anthropopathism is not the direct source of divine blessing. The direct source of blessing from God to mankind is the integrity of God, with emphasis on His justice.

A common misreading of 2 Corinthians 9:7 — 'God loves a cheerful giver' — illustrates the confusion. This is an anthropopathism. God does not love any person on the basis of emotional state or behavior. God loves only perfection; the divine attribute of love requires a perfect object. What the passage communicates in terms of divine policy is that the justice of God blesses those who give in accordance with their volition and capacity, not that cheerfulness as an emotional condition attracts divine favor.

III. Mankind's Point of Reference: The Justice of God

Since the fall of man, justice has been the operative category in God's relationship to the human race. At the fall, Adam was judged and the woman was judged — both by spiritual death. Each originated, through personal sin, his and her own old sin nature. The justice of God is the point of reference from which God deals with all of mankind.

A. The Fall and the Introduction of Justice

At the fall, the woman was deceived — her original sin was a sin of ignorance. The man acted in full cognizance — his sin was a sin of deliberate choice. The justice of God, however, operates on the principle of objective accountability: ignorance and cognizance are equally disqualifying. The woman sinned under deception; the man sinned knowingly. Both were pronounced guilty and both received spiritual death as the judicial consequence.

One significant doctrinal outcome of this distinction is the transmission of the old sin nature. Because the woman was deceived rather than acting in deliberate rebellion, she cannot contribute an old sin nature genetically. The old sin nature is therefore transmitted through the twenty-three male chromosomes. Both the man and the woman possessed old sin natures after the fall, but the genetic line of transmission runs exclusively through the male. This is the biological basis for the virgin birth: Christ, born of a woman without a human father, was not born with a genetically transmitted old sin nature.

B. The Priority of Justice Over Love

The most graphic demonstration that the justice of God is mankind's point of reference is the cross. In eternity past, the Father and the Holy Spirit loved the Son with a perfect, infinite, and eternal love — the divine attribute, never changing. Yet on the cross, when all the personal sins of the human race were imputed to Christ, the justice of God the Father judged those sins. Christ cried out: 'My God, my God, why have You forsaken Me?' — Matthew 27:46. The One who knew no sin was made sin for us (2 Corinthians 5:21), and the love that existed from eternity past, that will exist in eternity future, was superseded in that moment by the integrity of God acting in justice. The divine attribute of love did not change; it was not canceled. But the integrity of God — righteousness and justice — took absolute priority when sin was being judged. This is the definitive precedent: the justice of God is mankind's point of reference.

C. The Structure of Divine Integrity

The integrity or holiness of God is composed of two divine attributes: righteousness and justice. The fixed policy is: what righteousness demands, justice executes. Righteousness demands perfect righteousness; it rejects man's sinfulness. Justice demands justice; it pronounces the penalty of condemnation on what righteousness rejects. The love of God is subordinated to the integrity of God wherever mankind is in view.

This subordination does not mean love is irrelevant. Once a believer receives the imputation of divine righteousness at salvation, God loves the believer — not because of the believer's personality, merit, or behavior, but because God loves His own righteousness, and that righteousness now resides in the believer. This is the believer's first genuine contact with the divine attribute of love. Yet even at salvation, the love of God is not the point of reference. The point of reference remains the justice of God — which has now changed from a condemning function to a potential blessing function, because divine righteousness is present as the target for imputed blessing.

D. The Exclusion of Self-Righteousness

Imputed righteousness and human self-righteousness are mutually exclusive. The imputed righteousness of God is the sole basis for the imputation of blessing in time and in eternity. Self-righteousness, by contrast, brings cursing from the justice of God. These are not two points on a continuum; they are antithetical categories. To possess one is to exclude the other.

This principle has a direct application to Israel. The Jewish people repeatedly distorted the Mosaic Law into a system of self-righteousness, which excluded any blessing from the justice of God. This error — not ethnic identity, not national history — is the reason Paul's argument in Romans 9–11 must address Israel's condition so carefully. Self-righteousness is as great an obstacle to divine blessing as sinfulness, and in some respects greater, because it masquerades as compliance while in fact displacing the only category of righteousness God can bless.

IV. Human Failure and the Faithfulness of God

The fourth sub-paragraph of point thirteen introduces faithfulness as a manifestation of divine immutability. Human failure — individual or national — cannot cancel or neutralize the integrity of God.

A. The Principle

God's integrity is not canceled because some human beings reject Christ as Savior. God's integrity is not abrogated because believers fail to utilize logistical grace and advance to spiritual maturity. Mankind's lack of integrity does not neutralize God's integrity. Man may fail; God does not. Every generation of human history demonstrates this axiom.

B. Historical Illustration: France and the Huguenots

The history of France from the reign of Francis I through the Bourbon dynasty illustrates how human failure, however catastrophic, does not annul divine integrity but merely shifts the locus of blessing. Francis I, a gifted monarch, failed in his alliance with Henry VIII of England at the Field of the Cloth of Gold — a personal rivalry whose outcome redirected European geopolitics. His son Henry II died from a jousting wound before his reign could stabilize France. Catherine de' Medici, wife of Henry II, engineered a dynasty of three sons — all of whom persecuted the French Calvinist believers known as Huguenots, killing thousands. When that line expired, the Protestant Henry of Navarre (Henry IV, Bourbon) came to the throne and issued the Edict of Nantes guaranteeing religious liberty. That oath was subsequently broken under later Bourbon kings, and France never recovered the spiritual and political standing it might have held.

The principle, however, held. When Louis XIV persecuted the Huguenots, Frederick William, the Great Elector of Brandenburg-Prussia, opened his territory to the refugees. The pivot — the body of mature believers — was not destroyed; it was transferred. Brandenburg-Prussia, not France, became the beneficiary of that blessing. The justice of God is the source of both cursing and blessing; maladjustment to that justice in one national entity redirects blessing to another. Divine integrity is never neutral — it is always either blessing or cursing, never doing nothing.

C. The Integrity of God Defined

The integrity of God is infinite, absolute, eternal, and perfect — an integral part of His perfect essence. It is not the mere absence of evil or sin; it is the sum total of His perfection and incorruptibility. It is not maintained by His will or sovereignty, but by His immutable, unchangeable self. It is not supported by human ability, human talent, or self-righteousness.

Divine righteousness totally rejects human righteousness — they are mutually exclusive. Yet God in His grace provides all that His integrity demands of the human race, so that there will always be an option between grace and legalism. The option exists because God has acted first. The integrity of God stands eternally without any help from angels or mankind. God does not need human righteousness; humanity needs His.

D. Divine Integrity and the Glory of God

When the justice of God imputes blessing to the divine righteousness resident in the believer, God is glorified. This is a tactical victory in the angelic conflict. God is not glorified by human activity performed in order to earn divine approval. God is glorified when He can bless — when His justice finds divine righteousness as its target. The precedent is the cross: integrity superseded love in judging sin; now integrity supersedes all human effort in dispensing blessing.

Only God can glorify God. Only what God provides in grace brings the believer into the picture. Any maladjustment to the justice of God means no blessing from the justice of God, and therefore no glorification of God. This principle scales from the individual to the local assembly to the nation: no nation can possess freedom, prosperity, or blessing apart from the integrity of God. Social, economic, and political reform pursued apart from divine integrity intensifies problems rather than solving them, producing evil rather than restraining it.

V. Salvation Adjustment and the Foundation of Israel

Point fourteen of the Protocol Plan of God is introduced here as a bridge toward Romans 9:6–9. God's plan begins with salvation — adjustment to the justice of God through faith in the Lord Jesus Christ — which results in the imputation of divine righteousness, known theologically as justification.

Justification is not primarily a statement about man's standing before God in the courtroom sense, though that is included. More precisely, justification means that God is justified in blessing mankind. The believer possesses God's own righteousness; because God loves His righteousness, and that righteousness now resides in the believer, God is justified — His integrity is not compromised — in imputing blessing to that person. Justification therefore is the potential for great blessing from God both in time and in eternity.

When God establishes a dispensation in the human race, He begins with believers only. The foundation of the Jewish race was laid on regeneration: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were all believers, all of whom advanced to spiritual maturity. This established the precedent for Israel. Physical descent from Abraham was never sufficient to constitute membership in the covenant community in the full theological sense. Romans 9:6–7 states this explicitly: not all descended from Israel are really Israel; not all who are Abraham's physical descendants are children of the inheritance. The designation runs through Isaac — through the line of promise, which is the line of faith.

VI. The Pivot and the Preservation of the Jewish Race

The pivot principle — the body of mature believers within a nation whose adjustment to the justice of God sustains divine blessing on that nation — applies not only to Gentile client nations but to the preservation of the Jewish race across all generations of history.

A. The Remnant in Isaiah and Paul

In Isaiah 10:20–22, the prophet addresses the Assyrian crisis of 701 BC, when Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem. A remnant was formed — called in Hebrew שְׁאָר (shĕʾār), or in the more specific form שְׁאֵרִית (shĕʾērîth), the remnant or pivot. That remnant delivered Jerusalem and postponed Israel's fifth cycle of discipline by more than a century, from the Assyrian crisis to the Babylonian destruction of 586 BC.

When Paul quotes this passage in Romans 9:29 and 11:5, the Holy Spirit has him use the Greek term σπέρμα (sperma), meaning seed — specifically a spiritual seed. Paul cannot simply transliterate the Hebrew; he employs a term that carries the fuller theological freight of the New Testament context. Sperma denotes the regenerate remnant of Israel: those Jews in every generation who believe in the Lord Jesus Christ. The existence of this spiritual seed in every generation is what perpetuates the Jewish race.

B. The Spiritual Seed as Racial Preservation

Every Jewish believer who exists is evidence of the faithfulness of God. Every Jewish believer who advances to spiritual maturity becomes part of the pivot that protects the broader Jewish population. When the spiritual seed is large in a given generation, the Jewish people prosper and are protected from persecution. When it is small, historical catastrophe follows. The pattern is consistent across the entire history of Israel.

The tribulation period provides no exception to this principle. Throughout the times of the Gentiles and into the tribulation, there will always be a spiritual seed of Abraham — a regenerate remnant — and that remnant functions as the means of protecting the Jewish people as a race. The number of Jews in any generation and the severity of persecution they experience are directly correlated with the size and advancement of the spiritual seed in that generation.

This means that the greatest contribution any Jewish believer can make — for his nation, for his people, and for the angelic conflict — is to advance to spiritual maturity through consistent intake of Bible doctrine. Blessing by association flows from the pivot to the surrounding community, both nationally and racially. The principle that preserves a client nation is precisely the same principle that preserves the Jewish race through all of history.

Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Six

1. The divine attribute of love requires a perfect object. God does not fall in love, maintain love by an act of will, or express love through emotion. Because all human beings possess imputed sin, the old sin nature, and its manifestations, they are excluded from the divine attribute of love. Only a person who possesses divine righteousness — imputed at the moment of faith in Christ — becomes an object of the divine attribute of love.

2. Most scriptural references to God's love are anthropopathisms, not statements of the divine attribute. An anthropopathism is a human characteristic ascribed to God to explain His policy in terms of human frame of reference. John 3:16, Romans 5:8, and 2 Corinthians 9:7 employ the anthropopathism of love. The anthropopathism communicates divine motivation but must not be confused with the attribute itself.

3. Romans 9:13 requires the demonstrative force of the definite article. The clause 'Jacob I loved but Esau I hated' must be rendered: 'That Jacob I loved, but that Esau I hated.' Neither human love nor human hate is being predicated of God. Two antithetical anthropopathisms explain two antithetical divine policies: salvation adjustment to the justice of God versus rejection of Christ as Savior.

4. The justice of God, not the love of God, is mankind's point of reference. Since the fall, the integrity of God — composed of divine righteousness and divine justice — has been the operative category in God's relationship to the human race. What righteousness demands, justice executes. All blessing and all cursing flow from the same source: the justice of God.

5. The cross is the definitive demonstration that integrity supersedes love. The Father and the Holy Spirit loved the Son with an eternal, unchangeable, perfect love. Yet on the cross, when the sins of the human race were imputed to Christ, the justice of God judged those sins without exception. Love did not change; but integrity took absolute priority. The justice of God is therefore mankind's perpetual point of reference — for the Lord Jesus Christ in His humanity on the cross and for every human being thereafter.

6. Imputed righteousness and self-righteousness are mutually exclusive. The imputed righteousness of God received at salvation is the sole target for divine blessing in time and eternity. Self-righteousness displaces that target and brings cursing instead of blessing. Israel's distortion of the Mosaic Law into a self-righteousness system is the specific application Paul is building toward in Romans 9.

7. Human failure does not cancel or neutralize the integrity of God. Divine faithfulness is a function of divine immutability. When one national entity fails through maladjustment to the justice of God, the locus of blessing shifts to another. The transfer of the Huguenot pivot from France to Brandenburg-Prussia under the Great Elector illustrates that God always provides for His own; the failure is on the human side, never on the divine.

8. Justification means God is justified in blessing mankind. Justification is not primarily a declaration of the believer's standing in a courtroom; it is the provision of divine righteousness to the believer so that the justice of God can impute blessing to that righteousness without compromising divine integrity. The imputation of divine righteousness at salvation is the indispensable basis for all blessing in time and in eternity.

9. Physical descent from Abraham has never been the criterion for membership in the covenant community. Romans 9:6–7 establishes that not all descended from Israel are really Israel, and not all of Abraham's physical posterity are children of the inheritance. The line of promise runs through faith, not genetics. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were all believers who advanced to spiritual maturity — that is the foundation on which the nation was built.

10. The spiritual seed (sperma) is the mechanism of racial preservation for the Jewish people. Paul's use of σπέρμα (sperma) in Romans 9:29 and 11:5, drawn from the Hebrew shĕʾērîth (remnant) of Isaiah 10, identifies the regenerate remnant of Israel as the means by which the Jewish race is preserved in every generation. The size of this spiritual seed in any generation determines the degree of protection and blessing the broader Jewish population experiences. As goes the spiritual seed, so goes the Jewish race.

11. The pivot principle that preserves a client nation also preserves a race. The same mechanism — a body of mature believers whose adjustment to the justice of God sustains divine blessing on the surrounding community — operates both at the national level for Gentile client nations and at the racial level for Israel. Jewish believers who advance to spiritual maturity are therefore performing the highest service possible for their people: they constitute the spiritual seed that carries the race through every generation of history to the second advent.

anthrōpopatheia ἀνθρωποπάθεια anthrōpopatheia — anthropopathism A human characteristic ascribed to God to explain divine policy in terms comprehensible to the human frame of reference. God does not actually possess the characteristic; it functions as a descriptive analogy. Examples include divine love (John 3:16), divine hatred (Romans 9:13), divine wrath (Romans 1:18), and divine repentance. Anthropopathisms do not compromise divine integrity; they vindicate it by making divine policy accessible to finite understanding.

Because God loves His own righteousness, and that righteousness is now resident in the believer, the justice of God is free to impute blessing to the believer without compromising divine integrity. The central organizing concept of the Epistle to the Romans.
sperma σπέρμα sperma — seed; spiritual seed Used by Paul in Romans 9:29 and 11:5 to denote the regenerate remnant of Israel — those Jews in every generation who believe in the Lord Jesus Christ and advance to spiritual maturity. Paul employs this term in place of the Hebrew shĕʾērîth (remnant) of Isaiah 10 to convey the concept of a living, generative spiritual seed that perpetuates the Jewish race through all generations of history. The size of this seed in any generation determines the degree of protection and blessing experienced by the broader Jewish population.

Used in Isaiah 10:20–22 to designate the faithful remnant of Israel whose trust in the Lord during the Assyrian crisis of 701 BC formed the spiritual basis for Jerusalem's deliverance under Hezekiah. In Romans 9:29, Paul's use of the Greek sperma corresponds to this concept, extended to the entire span of Israel's history.
justification δικαίωσις dikaiōsis — justification; the act of declaring righteous The judicial act by which God imputes His own righteousness to the believer at the moment of saving faith. Imputed righteousness at salvation is the indispensable basis for all blessing in time and in eternity.

old sin nature (OSN) The sin capacity inherited at birth by every member of the human race, transmitted through the twenty-three male chromosomes. At the fall, both Adam and the woman acquired old sin natures through personal sin. Because the woman sinned in ignorance under deception, she cannot transmit the old sin nature genetically; the male line is the exclusive channel of transmission. All sins produced by the old sin nature were judged at the cross.

Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Seven

Romans 9:10 — The Case of Jacob and Esau: Election, Condemnation, and the Spiritual Seed

Romans 9:8–10 “This means that it is not the children of the flesh who are the children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as offspring. For this is what the promise said: 'About this time next year I will return, and Sarah shall have a son.' And not only so, but also when Rebekah had conceived children by one man, our forefather Isaac...” (ESV)
Corrected translation: This means that the descendants of the flesh — racial Jews — these are not the children of God; but the children of the promise are imputed for the spiritual seed. For the word of the promise is this: At this time — maturity adjustment to the justice of God — I will come to impute blessing, and Sarah will have a son. And not only this, but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac...

Romans 9 continues Paul's extended demonstration that the word of God has not failed with respect to Israel. The opening nine verses established the distinction between racial descent from Abraham and genuine membership in the spiritual Israel. Verse 10 introduces the second and more pointed case history: the twins Jacob and Esau, born of a single father and a single mother, yet representing opposite printouts from the computer of divine decrees. This chapter covers the concluding doctrinal material on the computer and condemnation (Point 14), the doctrine of the perfect plan of God, and the opening analysis of the Jacob-Esau case in verses 10 through 12.

I. The Computer and Condemnation (Point 14)

The previous sections established all the principles governing the computer of divine decrees as it relates to salvation — the omniscience of God feeding only actualities into the system, with positive volition at gospel hearing producing the printout of election, foreknowledge, and predestination. Point 14 addresses the complementary printout: condemnation.

A. Condemnation as the Printout of Negative Volition

Election, foreknowledge, and predestination are categories that apply exclusively to the believer. The unbeliever is never said to be predestined, foreknown in the redemptive sense, or elected. These are terms reserved for those who possess divine righteousness through faith in Christ. The omniscience of God does, however, feed into the computer of divine decrees all information regarding the unbeliever. The simple categorical label for that printout is condemnation.

The justice of God condemns the unbeliever both in time and in eternity. Condemnation in time deals with the individual personally and also with the individual as a member of a group — judgment can be both personal and corporate. Condemnation in eternity is the permanent state of separation from God. Neither form of condemnation is a function of divine sovereignty operating apart from human choice. It is a function of the free will, the self-determination, and the free agency of the individual.

B. The Racial Jew and the Condemnation Printout

This principle becomes critical for the interpretation of Romans 9. The racial Jew who does not become the regenerate Jew — the physical seed of Abraham who rejects Christ as Savior and substitutes self-righteousness derived from law-keeping — always prints out condemnation. He is not among the people of God. He does not receive the imputation of the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, or New Covenants to Israel. Physical descent from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is necessary but not sufficient for inclusion in the election of Israel.

Hosea expressed this with compressed precision: לֹא עַמִּי (lo' ammi) — not my people. The racial Jew who rejects Christ is not the people of God. The born-again Jew is the people of God. This is the consistent testimony of Hosea 1:10 and 2:23, passages Paul will deploy directly in the course of this chapter.

The condemnation information exists in the computer of divine decrees, but it is never classified under election, foreknowledge, and predestination. It is filed under a separate category: condemnation. The two printouts are distinct. God did not predestine anyone to condemnation; He simply knew, with infinite precision, how every individual's volition would function at the point of gospel hearing and God-consciousness, and that knowledge was fed as fact into the divine system.

II. The Doctrine of the Perfect Plan of God

A. The Wheel and the Axle

The plan of God has existed from eternity past. No believer is ever commanded to reinvent it. The wheel is a useful image: the plan of God keeps rolling regardless of what any individual or generation does, because it rests on the character of God Himself. What matters is the axle on which that wheel turns.

The axle is divine righteousness — the imputed righteousness of God (

The axle on which the wheel of the Christian life must turn is divine righteousness — the imputed righteousness of God, +R. At the moment of salvation, God imputes one half of His divine integrity — His righteousness — to the believer. This imputed righteousness becomes the home, the target, for all subsequent divine blessing. Without it, God cannot bless. Without it, there is no future, no eternity with God, no definition to life, no meaning or purpose for existence on this planet.

B. Two Axle Choices

Every believer must choose an axle. The choice is binary. Either the believer accepts the axle God has provided — imputed divine righteousness — or he manufactures his own axle, which is some form of self-righteousness. Choosing self-righteousness means dictating to God the terms of His own plan. It means insisting that keeping the Ten Commandments obligates God to save, that tithing obligates God to bless, that witnessing to a certain number of people per day obligates God to reward. None of these assumptions hold. The assumption that divine blessing is produced by human performance is the error that underlies every form of legalism and every system of works-righteousness.

Prayer is commanded in Scripture. Witnessing is commanded in Scripture. Giving is commanded in Scripture. But none of these are a source of blessing. They are the expression of a life already positioned under grace, not the mechanism by which grace is obtained. The imputation of divine righteousness at salvation is the definitive divine statement on this point: God set it up. God did it. The axle is His.

C. Two Post-Salvation Volition Tracks

Beyond the salvation adjustment, a second great issue of volition presents itself: the believer's response to Bible doctrine. Positive volition toward the intake of doctrine over time produces advance through the spiritual life — cracking the maturity barrier, moving through supergrace into ultra-supergrace. Negative volition toward doctrine produces reversionism, with warning discipline, intensive discipline, and ultimately dying discipline. The life of the reversionist is marked by disorientation to reality, inflexibility on non-essentials combined with flexibility on essentials, and the progressive substitution of self-righteousness for the righteousness of God.

The perfect plan of God excludes human ability, human personality, human morality, human works, human ideas, and human schemes. There is nothing a person can do — now or ever — to generate blessing from God by personal effort. What God did for Abraham He does for every believer at salvation: He imputes His righteousness, and that imputed righteousness becomes the permanent basis on which all subsequent blessing in time and eternity is dispensed.

III. Review of the Corrected Translation: Romans 9:1–9

Before moving to verse 10, the chapter provides a consolidated corrected translation of the first nine verses as a baseline for what follows.

Romans 9:1–9 — Corrected Translation “” (ESV)
Corrected translation: I am communicating doctrine; I am not lying — my conscience bearing joint testimony with me in the Holy Spirit — that I have a great sorrow and constant pain in my right lobe. For I could wish that I myself would be accursed — consequently separated from Christ — it cannot be. For the sake of my brethren, racial Jews, my fellow countrymen, national Jews, according to earthly descent — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob — who are Israelites, to whom is the adoption and the Shekinah glory and the unconditional covenants and the gift of the law and the worship of the true God and the promises from the integrity of God. From whom are the regenerate ancestors — Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. In fact, from whom is the Christ, the one who came in the flesh, the one who is God, ruler over all, extolled, praised, eulogized forever — Amen. However, this is not to imply that the word of God has failed, for not all who are really descended from Israel are really Israel. All Israel is not Israel. Neither because they are Abraham's posterity — that is, his physical seed — are all racial Jews children of the inheritance. But [quoting Genesis 21:12]: In Isaac, your posterity shall be elected. This means that the descendants of the flesh — racial Jews, genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — these are not the children of God, but the children of the promise are imputed for the spiritual seed. For the word of the promise is this [quoting Genesis 18:10]: At this time — maturity adjustment to the justice of God — I will come to impute blessing, and Sarah will have a son.

IV. The Case of Jacob and Esau: Romans 9:10–12

A. The First Case History Reviewed: Ishmael and Isaac

The opening of verse 10 — "and not only this" — is a post-positive conjunctive particle (

The opening of verse 10 — "and not only this" — uses the post-positive conjunctive particle δέ (de) combined with the negative adverb οὐ (ou) and the adverb μόνον (monon, from the adjective μόνος, monos — alone, only), used here as an accusative of respect functioning adverbially. The phrase signals a transition from the first case history — Ishmael and Isaac — to the second.

Human viewpoint might raise an objection to the first case history. Ishmael was excluded from the line of promise; Isaac was included. One might argue that the distinction was social or genealogical: Ishmael's mother Hagar was an Egyptian slave, while Isaac's mother Sarah was Abraham's legitimate wife. On this reading, Ishmael's exclusion was a function of illegitimate birth, and Isaac's inclusion was a function of legal standing. But this objection misses the actual ground of distinction. Ishmael's own self-determination as a mature individual — his negative volition toward the God of his father — is what eliminated him from the line. Isaac's gentle, thoughtful character also had nothing to do with his inclusion. Character, social standing, maternal lineage, and order of birth are all irrelevant to the transmission of divine promises.

B. The Second Case History: Twins from One Father and One Mother

The second illustration removes every remaining human variable. In the Ishmael-Isaac case, one could point to different mothers and different social circumstances. The case of Jacob and Esau eliminates even that objection. Same father: Isaac. Same mother: Rebekah. Same womb. Same moment of conception. Yet one twin prints out as elect and the other prints out as condemned.

The physical differences between the twins were observable — one was notably hairy at birth, the other was not; their temperaments differed markedly — but these physical and temperamental distinctions are not the ground of the theological distinction Paul is making. Esau was personally courageous, direct, and tough. Jacob was cautious, indirect, and resourceful. But the decisive difference was neither courage nor character. The decisive difference was spiritual: Jacob believed in the Lord and was imputed divine righteousness and eternal life. Esau did not believe in the Lord and carried self-righteousness — minus R — throughout his life.

C. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Plus R

The origin of the Jewish race is itself an act of divine imputation. Abraham was not a Jew by birth. He was a Gentile — a Sumero-Akkadian from Ur of the Chaldeans. He believed in the Lord, and divine righteousness was imputed to him. He remained ethnically a Gentile, but he now possessed divine righteousness. When he cracked the maturity barrier — spiritually mature, sexually dead for thirteen years, his wife Sarah ninety years old and post-menopausal — God imputed to him the major blessing of supernatural physical restoration, so that the promised son could be conceived and born. The Jewish race began as an imputation of divine blessing to imputed divine righteousness. The line could only be continued through those who also possessed that righteousness.

This is why the line passed through Isaac and not Ishmael: Isaac had +R; Ishmael had −R. God cannot impute covenant blessing to self-righteousness. He can only impute blessing to His own righteousness. The same principle governs the Jacob-Esau distinction. Jacob had +R; Esau had −R. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob share one common denominator as the patriarchal foundation of the Jewish race: all three possessed imputed divine righteousness. The line of racial Israel is inseparable from the line of spiritual Israel at its origin.

D. The Computer of Divine Decrees: Jacob and Esau

Billions of years before creation, the omniscience of God knew — with the precision that characterizes infinite knowledge — that Esau would reject Christ as Savior and that Jacob would believe in the Lord. This knowledge was fed as fact into the computer of divine decrees. Probability — what would have happened had Esau been the believer and Jacob the unbeliever — exists in the omniscience of God as alternative knowledge, but it was not fed into the computer as fact because it did not occur. Only actuality enters the computer.

The resulting printouts are straightforward. Jacob: election, foreknowledge, predestination — the full category of blessing associated with divine righteousness and eternal life. Esau: condemnation — in time, in the historical consequences of his choices, and in eternity. God's omniscience has nothing to do with coercing either printout. He simply knew with absolute certainty how each man's free will would function. Predestination, foreordination, and election are categories that presuppose the possession of imputed divine righteousness. They are inapplicable to the unbeliever. Esau was not predestined to condemnation; he was condemned because he rejected the Savior. The condemnation printout is the system's accurate record of that rejection.

Esau later wept and sought his birthright with tears, as recorded in Hebrews. Emotional response — however intense, however sincere in its expression of desire for what was lost — cannot substitute for faith in the Lord. The birthright demanded divine righteousness as its prerequisite. Esau did not possess it. Tears of repentance, however genuine as an emotional event, do not generate the imputed righteousness of God. Only faith in Christ accomplishes that.

V. Paul's Concern for Racial Israel

The theological precision of this chapter illuminates the depth of Paul's concern expressed in Romans 9:1–3. The Jews who remained as a national entity after the ascension of Christ in AD 30 continued as a client nation to God for forty years — long enough for the prophetic sign of tongues to fulfill its warning function, evangelizing Jewish audiences in Gentile languages to signal impending divine discipline. Paul himself was the last great Jewish missionary of that client nation, the apostle through whom the Gentile nations would receive the doctrinal foundation for the times of the Gentiles.

Paul's concern is not sentimental. It is rooted in the recognition that the Jews who reject Christ are rejecting the very thing that constitutes the origin of their race — divine imputation of righteousness through faith. They are racial Jews, physically descended from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but they are not spiritual Jews. They are not the people of God. They are not in the election of Israel. The Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, and New Covenants will be imputed to Israel — but to the Israel that possesses divine righteousness and eternal life, not to the racial community that has substituted law-keeping and self-righteousness for faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, the Shekinah glory, the God of Israel, Jehovah Elohim.

After the fifth cycle of discipline fell on the Jewish nation in AD 70 — two years after Paul's death — no Jewish nation could serve as a client nation to God until the Second Advent. The times of the Gentiles require Gentile client nations. Evangelism of the Jews would thenceforth flow from Gentile believers to Jewish individuals, reversing the direction of the missionary movement that had characterized the apostolic generation.

Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Seven

1. Physical descent is worthless for the transmission of divine promises. Natural birth into the racial lineage of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob does not qualify a person to receive the imputation of divine blessing. The transmission of divine promises requires imputed divine righteousness, which is obtained only through faith in Christ. This does not preclude blessing by association, but the direct line of covenant fulfillment runs through the spiritual seed, not the physical seed.

2. Only salvation adjustment to the justice of God can qualify the racial Jew as an elect Jew. The election of Israel is inseparable from the imputation of divine righteousness at salvation. A racial Jew who rejects Christ as Savior is not under election, foreknowledge, or predestination. He is under condemnation — in time and in eternity — because his volition at the point of gospel hearing has been negative.

3. The computer of divine decrees feeds only on actuality, not on probability. The omniscience of God knows both what has occurred and every alternative that did not occur. But only actuality is fed into the computer of divine decrees as the basis for the printouts of election and condemnation. God did not coerce Jacob's faith or Esau's unbelief. He knew these facts with absolute certainty from eternity past, and the decrees reflect that knowledge.

4. Election, foreknowledge, and predestination are categories that apply exclusively to believers. The unbeliever is never said to be predestined or foreknown in the redemptive sense. These categories presuppose the possession of imputed divine righteousness. Condemnation is a separate printout category, filed independently, and is always the result of the individual's own free-will rejection of Christ.

5. The origin of the Jewish race is itself an act of divine imputation. Abraham was a Gentile who believed in the Lord. Divine righteousness was imputed to him. The Jewish race began when God imputed supernatural blessing to that imputed righteousness, restoring Abraham's physical capacity to father a child after cracking the maturity barrier. The perpetuation of that race through Isaac and Jacob — and not through Ishmael or Esau — follows the same logic: only those who possess divine righteousness can serve as the conduit of covenant blessing.

6. The wheel of God's plan must turn on the axle of imputed divine righteousness. The plan of God has existed from eternity past and cannot be reinvented by human effort. Self-righteousness — whether through law-keeping, tithing, witnessing, or any other human performance — is the wrong axle. It cannot bear the weight of divine blessing because God can only impute blessing to His own righteousness, not to the believer's performance. Positive volition toward doctrine, sustained over time, advances the believer toward the maturity barrier and beyond — but always on the axle of imputed divine righteousness, never on the axle of self.

7. The true Israel is the spiritual seed, not the physical seed. Not all who are descended from Israel are Israel. The born-again Jew is the people of God. The racial Jew who rejects Christ is not. This is the consistent testimony of Hosea, confirmed by Paul in Romans 9 and elaborated through the twin case histories of Ishmael-Isaac and Jacob-Esau. Paul's grief in 9:1–3 is the grief of a man who understands both the privilege conferred by racial descent and the tragedy of a people who have exchanged their covenant heritage for a self-righteousness that the justice of God cannot honor.

8. Emotional response cannot substitute for faith in Christ. Esau sought his birthright with tears. The emotional intensity of his appeal was real. The desire for what he had forfeited was genuine. But tears of repentance, however sincere, do not produce the imputation of divine righteousness. Only faith in the Lord Jesus Christ accomplishes that. Every system that grounds acceptance before God in emotional experience — grief over sin, intensity of desire, earnestness of prayer — misunderstands the nature of the adjustment to the justice of God.

The divine decree that marks out in advance the destiny of the believer who possesses imputed divine righteousness. katakrima κατάκριμα katakrima — condemnation, judgment against From kata (against, down) + krino (to judge). The adverse judicial verdict of God's justice against the unbeliever, both in time and in eternity.
